ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $BC=120$, the height $AD=60$, and the square $EFGH$ with one side on $BC$, points $E$, $F$ respectively on $AB$, $AC$, $AD$ intersects $EF$ at point $N$, what is the length of $AN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the side lengths of square EFGH be EF = EH = x,\\
since EFGH is a square,\\
thus $\angle$HEF = $\angle$EHG = $90^\circ$, and EF$\parallel$BC,\\
thus $\triangle$AEF $\sim$ $\triangle$ABC,\\
since AD is the altitude of $\triangle$ABC,\\
thus $\angle$HDN = $90^\circ$,\\
thus quadrilateral EHDN is a rectangle,\\
thus DN = EH = x,\\
since $\triangle$AEF $\sim$ $\triangle$ABC,\\
thus $\frac{AN}{AD}=\frac{EF}{BC}$ (the ratio of altitudes is equal to the scale factor),\\
since BC = 120, AD = 60,\\
thus AN = 60−x,\\
thus $\frac{60−x}{60}$ = $\frac{x}{120}$,\\
solving for x gives: x = 40,\\
thus AN=60−x=60−40=\boxed{20}.

Since $EFGH$ is a square, $\angle HEF=\angle EHG=90^\circ$, and $EF\parallel BC$, so $\triangle AEF \sim \triangle ABC$. Since $AD$ is the altitude of $\triangle ABC$, $\angle HDN=90^\circ$, so quadrilateral $EHDN$ is a rectangle. Thus $DN=EH=x$. Since $\triangle AEF \sim \triangle ABC$, we have $\frac{AN}{AD}=\frac{EF}{BC}$ (the ratio of altitudes is equal to the scale factor). Since $BC=120$ and $AD=60$, we also have $AN=60-x$. Thus $\frac{60-x}{60}=\frac{x}{120}$. Solving gives $x=40$, so $AN=60-40=\boxed{20}$.

Square EFGH is located inside the triangle, HG is on BC, E is on AB, F is on AC, EF is horizontal and parallel to BC. AD intersects EF at N. The problem gives BC=120, AD=60.

Reasoning: Let the side length of the square be x, then EF=EH=x. Because EF is parallel to BC, triangle AEF and triangle ABC are similar, and the ratio of corresponding heights equals the ratio of corresponding sides, so AN/AD=EF/BC=x/120. Also because the square has height x upward from BC, and AD is perpendicular to BC, the vertical distance DN from D to EF is x, so AN=AD-DN=60-x.
